vibe.title: Vibe Check
vibe.content:
SLOW JAM: MICHAEL BUBLÉ, "HOME" (2005)
• STAT: No. 1 on Billboard's Adult Contemporary chart in the U.S. (No. 72 on the Hot 100).
• WHY TODAY: The biggest travel week of the year starts now, and this is the song about wanting to get home. Bublé co-wrote it while touring Italy, missing his then-fiancée.
😂 JOKES: Bublé wrote 'Home' while touring Italy. I'd miss home too, if home had my mom's stuffing. / This song is for everybody driving to Grandma's. And the one guy still on the US-31 shoulder looking for his phone.

🚗 DRIVE TEASE: Cold and quiet for the drive in. About 28 at 6 AM and 29 by 8 under partly sunny skies, with calm wind. Wet roads refroze overnight, so watch for slick spots on bridges and overpasses.

📅 THIS DAY: GANGNAM STYLE TAKES OVER YOUTUBE (NOV. 24, 2012)
• On this date in 2012, PSY's 'Gangnam Style' passed Justin Bieber's 'Baby' to become the most-viewed video on YouTube, with more than 803 million views.
• Less than a month later, on Dec. 21, 2012, it became the first YouTube video ever to hit a billion views.
• Somewhere, every wedding DJ in America did the horse dance in celebration.
😂 JOKES: Every uncle at every 2012 wedding did that horse dance. Some of them are still doing it. Nobody has told them. / A billion views. My best YouTube video is me trying to fix a garbage disposal, and it has 11, nine of them from my mom.

💡 FUN FACT: IT'S NATIONAL SARDINES DAY
• The word 'sardine' probably comes from the island of Sardinia, where the fish were once supposedly plentiful.
• And there isn't one sardine. The international standard for canned sardines lists 21 different species that can be sold as sardines.
😂 JOKES: Twenty-one kinds of sardines, and they all fit in the same little can. That's my family's minivan on the way to Grandma's. / Packed in like sardines is also how they describe Meijer at 6 AM Friday.

🎉 NATIONAL DAYS: National Sardines Day · Celebrate Your Unique Talent Day

GOOD MORNING UP NORTH: Cold, quiet and partly sunny. About 28 at 6 AM, a high near 39 this afternoon with light west wind, then mostly cloudy tonight, low 25. Wednesday high near 41, and Thanksgiving Day looks mostly cloudy, high near 45, with the holiday travel window dry.

SCHOOLS: No closings or delays listed this morning.

ROADS: Wet roads refroze overnight. Watch for slick spots, especially on bridges and overpasses. No verified closures.

ENERGY: Short week, giving week. Toys for Tots is rolling, the corn's almost in, and everybody's one grocery run from done.

mood.content:
MOOD BOOST: VANESSA CARLTON, "A THOUSAND MILES" (2002)
• STAT: Peaked at No. 5 on the Billboard Hot 100 for three weeks in May 2002 and stayed on the chart 41 weeks.
• STORY: She wrote the piano riff in 1998 at her parents' house, and her mom heard it and said, 'Vanessa, that's a hit song.' It was first called 'Interlude' until the label president insisted on a new title.
• WHY TODAY: Everybody's driving a thousand miles this week. Or at least it feels like it on US-131.
😂 JOKES: Mom called it a hit in 1998. My mom called my garage band 'loud' in 1998. Same energy, different results. / They almost named it 'Interlude.' Nobody's walking a thousand miles for a song called 'Interlude.'

buzz.title: Daily Buzz
buzz.content:
━━ LOCAL ━━

⭐ TOYS FOR TOTS IS ROLLING: KICKOFF HAULS IN THOUSANDS OF TOYS
• SUMMARY: The Toys for Tots campaign in northwest Michigan kicked off Saturday with a drive-through toy drive at Fox Grand Traverse, and thousands of toys came in on day one. The campaign now runs through Friday, Dec. 11, with more than 100 drop-off spots.
• THE CATCH: Last year organizers handed out 26,000 toys to more than 6,000 kids in Grand Traverse, Benzie, Kalkaska, Leelanau and Antrim counties, so day one is just the warm-up.
• WHO: The Marine Corps Reserve's Toys for Tots, 79 years old, with 800 campaigns in all 50 states. WHAT: Toy drive. WHERE: 100-plus drop-off spots across five counties. WHEN: Now through Dec. 11. WHY IT MATTERS: Black Friday is Friday, so it's the easiest time all year to grab one extra toy.
➜ TAKE: If you're out shopping Friday anyway, buy one for you and one for the bin. That's the whole plan.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what was the toy you wanted most as a kid? Did Santa come through?
😂 JOKES: The Marines are collecting toys. Finally, a drill sergeant who yells, 'Drop and give me a Barbie.' / Thousands of toys in one day at a car dealership. Easiest test drive those guys ever did.

A BAKING SHOW CHAMP IS COMING TO SUTTONS BAY
• SUMMARY: Martin Sorge, who won The Great American Baking Show, will teach two hands-on holiday baking classes at the Inn at Black Star Farms in Suttons Bay this December. On Dec. 5 from noon to 2 p.m. it's holiday cookies, and on Dec. 12 from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. it's traditional German stollen.
• THE CATCH: You leave with a box of cookies or a loaf of stollen, plus the recipes, so you can pretend you made them all along.
• WHO: Martin Sorge, Great American Baking Show winner. WHAT: Two holiday classes, with his cookbook Great Bakes for sale and signing. WHERE: The Inn at Black Star Farms, Suttons Bay. WHEN: Dec. 5 and Dec. 12. WHY IT MATTERS: It's his third visit to Black Star Farms this year, and holiday baking season starts the second the turkey's gone.
➜ TAKE: A TV baking champ teaching you cookies in Leelanau County. That beats my method, which is buying the tube of dough and eating half of it raw.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what's the one holiday cookie your family can't live without?
😂 JOKES: Stollen is a German fruit bread. Not to be confused with 'stolen,' which is what happens to the last cookie at my house. / He won a baking show. I won a staring contest with a box of Little Debbies. Same energy.

TROOPERS BUY WINTER COATS AND BOOTS FOR 55 TCAPS KIDS
• SUMMARY: The Eagles-for-Children program gave a $6,000 grant to the Michigan State Police STOP program, and troopers used it to buy winter gear for 55 TCAPS elementary students. That's coats, snow pants and boots, just as the snow starts to stick.
• THE CATCH: STOP stands for State-Trooper-Outreach-Partnership, and since 2016 it's run Boots for Kids and Coats for Kids, plus bike helmets and life jackets in summer.
• WHO: MSP troopers and Eagles-for-Children. WHAT: Winter gear for 55 kids. WHERE: TCAPS elementary schools. WHY IT MATTERS: Trooper Miranda Swanson said nobody wants to see a kid going down the road in a frigid Up North winter without the right gear.
➜ TAKE: Troopers in boot-buying mode. Pretty sure that's the only time a kid's happy to see a state cop pull up.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487 a shout-out to somebody who quietly takes care of kids in your town.
😂 JOKES: A state trooper fitting a first grader for snow boots. That's the only time 'license and registration' means 'left foot and right foot.' / Fifty-five kids, fifty-five pairs of boots, and somewhere one mitten already missing. That's just science.

GLEN ARBOR LIGHTS UP THIS WEEKEND FOR LEELANAU TEENS
• SUMMARY: The sixth annual Strolling Lights Festival comes to Glen Arbor this weekend, Saturday and Sunday, Nov. 28 and 29, as Crystal River Outfitters fills its corner of town with decorated holiday trees. This year the festival benefits LIFT, Leelanau Investing for Teens.
• THE CATCH: Anybody can sponsor and decorate a tree for $150, families and groups included, and the trees stay up for strolling through the holidays.
• WHO: Crystal River Outfitters and LIFT. WHAT: A walk-through holiday tree festival. WHERE: Crystal River Outfitters Recreational District, Glen Arbor. WHEN: Nov. 28 and 29. WHY IT MATTERS: LIFT runs free after-school programs for 6th through 12th graders at Suttons Bay, Glen Lake, Leland and Northport.
➜ TAKE: Thanksgiving weekend plan: eat Thursday, shop Friday, stroll Glen Arbor Saturday, nap Sunday. You're welcome.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: when does your tree go up? Before Thanksgiving, the day after, or are you a December 24th person?
😂 JOKES: A festival where you just walk and look at lights. Finally, a holiday event my cardio can handle. / Decorate a tree for teens. Which means somebody's hanging a phone charger on it.

CORN HARVEST NEARLY DONE: GT FARM REPORTS 'PHENOMENAL YIELDS'
• SUMMARY: Long Acre Farms in Grand Traverse County is about 90% through its corn harvest, and owner Matt Breithaupt says timely rains plus a long dry fall gave them phenomenal yields. He hopes to wrap up by the end of this week.
• THE CATCH: Fuel prices have taken a toll the last four months, he says, on everything from parts to tires to chains. And with no snow cover yet, the winter wheat could be at risk.
• WHO: Matt Breithaupt, Long Acre Farms. WHAT: A strong corn year. WHERE: Grand Traverse County. WHY IT MATTERS: His line, 'It's not about how much rain we get, it's a matter of when,' is the most Up North weather wisdom you'll hear all week.
➜ TAKE: Farmers rooting for snow and everybody else rooting against it. Thanksgiving week, pick a side.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: corn on the Thanksgiving table, yes or no? Creamed, kernel or cornbread?
😂 JOKES: Ninety percent done by Thanksgiving. That's more than I can say for my gutters. / Phenomenal yields. My garden's yield this year was one zucchini, and it was the size of a canoe.

━━ NATIONAL ━━

TAYLOR SWIFT SURPRISES BRENDA LEE WITH A DIAMOND
• SUMMARY: Taylor Swift surprised Brenda Lee, 81, in Nashville with an RIAA Diamond plaque for 'Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree,' certified for more than 10 million units in the U.S. The video of the moment came out Monday.
• THE CATCH: It's only the second holiday song ever to go Diamond, joining Mariah Carey's 'All I Want for Christmas Is You.'
• WHO: Taylor Swift and Brenda Lee. WHAT: Diamond certification. WHERE: Nashville. WHEN: Presented Nov. 16, video out Nov. 23. WHY IT MATTERS: Lee recorded that song as a teenager, and it still owns December.
➜ TAKE: Mariah, scoot over. There's another queen on the Christmas throne, and she's 81.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what's the first Christmas song you allow yourself to play? And is it too early?
😂 JOKES: Ten million units. My Christmas playlist has ten million units too, and they're all Mariah. / Taylor Swift handing out awards now. Next week she's delivering my mail.

━━ BITS ━━

BIT: CELEBRATE YOUR UNIQUE TALENT DAY
• It's Celebrate Your Unique Talent Day, per the National Day Calendar. Not the talent on your resume. The weird one.
• Can you touch your nose with your tongue? Name every Taylor Swift album in order? Parallel park a minivan in one try on Front Street in July?
• Pair it with the Dry Bar 'most useless talent' clip in Trending Audio.
➜ TAKE: Mine is knowing exactly when the microwave is about to beep and stopping it at one second so nobody wakes up.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487 your weirdest talent. Best one gets read on air.
😂 JOKES: My unique talent is falling asleep in any recliner within four minutes. Thanksgiving is my Olympics. / I can also burp the alphabet, but this is a family show, so we'll leave that one in the garage.

BIT: WHEN ARE YOU ROLLING IN FOR THANKSGIVING?
• UpNorthLive is asking its viewers a simple one this week: when do you plan to arrive at your Thanksgiving destination?
• Are you the Wednesday-night early bird, the Thursday 'we'll be there by noon' liar, or the person who shows up right when the turkey hits the table?
• With slick spots on bridges this morning, AJ's vote: leave early, drive slow.
➜ TAKE: There are two kinds of Thanksgiving guests: the ones who help set the table, and the ones who show up with a bag of ice like it's a casserole.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what time are you really getting there?
😂 JOKES: 'We'll be there at noon' is the most-told lie of Thanksgiving. Right after 'I'm not that hungry.' / If you show up after the dishes are done, you're not a guest. You're a leftover.

━━ SPORTS ━━

LIONS: BEARS ON THANKSGIVING, 1 PM, CBS
• Lions host the Bears Thursday at Ford Field. Kickoff 1 PM, on CBS and Paramount+.
• Monday's injury estimate: Sam LaPorta limited (ankle). Chuck Clark, Skyler Gill-Howard, Ennis Rakestraw Jr. and DJ Wonnum did not participate. D.J. Reed and Khalil Dorsey full.
• Rundown: Detroit is coming off a 31-21 win over Tampa Bay.

lifestyle.title: Lifestyle & Trends
lifestyle.content:
BLACK FRIDAY TURNOUT HITS A 10-YEAR HIGH
• Deloitte's new survey says 87% of shoppers plan to hit Black Friday through Cyber Monday deals this year, the most since 2016.
• Average planned spend is $624, flat with last year, and 72% are holding some purchases for the deals.
• Gen Z is all in: 94% plan to shop the week and spend 23% more.
➜ LOCAL ANGLE: Up here that means Meijer at dawn, Cherryland or the Grand Traverse Mall, then a hot cocoa downtown. Small Business Saturday is right behind it.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: are you a 5 AM doorbuster or a Cyber Monday couch shopper?
😂 JOKES: Seventy-two percent are waiting for the deal. The other 28% are my wife, who already bought everything in August. / Gen Z is spending 23% more. On what? I don't know. I asked my nephew and he said 'it's giving' and walked away.

SIDES BEAT THE BIRD: AMERICA WOULD RATHER COOK THE SIDES
• Campbell's 2026 State of the Sides report surveyed 5,017 Americans, and 80% would rather cook the side dishes than the turkey.
• The top five sides haven't changed in three years: green bean casserole, mac and cheese, yams or sweet potatoes, mashed potatoes, and stuffing or dressing.
➜ LOCAL ANGLE: Up North we'd add a cherry something, a jello salad nobody admits to making, and somebody's grandma's pie.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what side HAS to be on your table, or it's not Thanksgiving?
😂 JOKES: Eighty percent would rather make the sides. The other 20% are the guys standing by the turkey holding a meat thermometer like it's a lightsaber. / Stuffing or dressing is the only Thanksgiving argument where both sides are right and both sides are bread.

officeschool.content:
OFFICE: THE HARDEST-WORKING OFFICE IN AMERICA THIS WEEK
• The Butterball Turkey Talk-Line has more than 50 culinary experts on the phones right now, answering questions on thawing, roasting, doneness and leftovers.
• It started in 1981, it's open through Dec. 24, and you can call 1-800-BUTTERBALL, text, email or chat.
➜ TAKE: Your office thinks Monday's busy. Imagine Thursday morning at Butterball: 'Ma'am, the turkey is still frozen. Put down the hair dryer.'
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what's the worst question you've ever gotten at work?
😂 JOKES: It even got a West Wing episode. That's more TV time than my whole department. / Their busiest day is Thanksgiving. Mine is the day after, when I eat lunch over the sink.

OFFICE: THE SHORT-WEEK OFFICE, RANKED
• It's a two-and-a-half-day week for a lot of offices, and everybody plays a role.
• There's the coworker who's 'out of office' since Friday, the one with a slow cooker under the desk, and the one asking 'are we doing anything for Thanksgiving?' in a group text at 4:59.
➜ TAKE: Short-week rule: if a meeting can be an email, and the email can be a 'happy Thanksgiving,' do that.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what's your office doing this short week? Potluck? Ghost town?
😂 JOKES: Nobody does real work the Wednesday before Thanksgiving. We just move files from one folder to another and call it 'getting ahead.' / The office potluck sign-up sheet: six people bringing chips, one brave soul bringing a casserole, and Kevin bringing napkins. Again.

SCHOOL: THE GREAT THANKSGIVING BREAK DEBATE
• School calendars are getting surveyed everywhere, and Thanksgiving break is one of the big fights.
• Colorado's District 49 just asked more than 2,200 parents, students and staff about eight parts of the calendar, and Thanksgiving break was one of them.
➜ TAKE: Full week off or just Wednesday through Friday? Parents, this is where you find out what your kids really eat in a day.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: Thanksgiving break, full week or short break? Parents and teachers, settle it.
😂 JOKES: A full week off with the kids. Day one: 'This is great.' Day three: 'Is the school open for visitors?' / Teachers love Thanksgiving break, because it's the one time they get to eat lunch sitting down.

SCHOOL: THE HANDPRINT TURKEY HALL OF FAME
• It's Thanksgiving craft week in a lot of classrooms: handprint turkeys, paper Pilgrim hats, and the 'I am thankful for' sheet.
• Parents, those sheets are honest. Some kids are thankful for family. Some are thankful for their dog, pizza and Wi-Fi, in that order.
➜ TAKE: Keep every handprint turkey. In 20 years it's the only proof your kid's hand was ever that small.
➜ BAIT: Text 231-929-4487: what's the funniest thing your kid said they're thankful for?
😂 JOKES: My kid's thankful sheet said 'Mom, Dad and the iPad.' I'm just glad I beat the iPad. Barely. / A handprint turkey is the only art on my fridge that's appreciated in value.

mental.title: Mental Health Minute
mental.content:
SAVOR ONE GOOD THING FOR TWENTY SECONDS

It's the start of Thanksgiving week, and if your brain already feels like a grocery list, you're in good company. Between the travel, the cooking and the slick bridges this morning, it's easy to rush right past the good stuff. So here's one small move for today. When something good happens, like the first sip of coffee, a kid's laugh in the back seat, or the sun coming up over the bay, stop and stay with it for about twenty seconds. Notice what you see and how it feels, because researchers who tracked people's days found that the days they savored their good moments were the days they felt happier. It costs nothing, it works in a warm kitchen, and you can do it at a red light. Try it once this morning, and then text us at 231-929-4487 and tell us the one good thing you savored today.

https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/17439760.2012.671345
Jose, Lim & Bryant (2012), J. Positive Psychology 7(3): daily diary study linking savoring of positive events with higher daily happiness. Indoor move (no walking) for icy roads.

cross.content:
CROSS TALK: MEET THE PARENTS, THANKSGIVING EDITION
• 'Focker In-Law' opens in theaters Wednesday, the fourth movie in the Meet the Parents series, with Ariana Grande joining Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro, 16 years after the last one.
• Early reviews are rough on the movie but kind to Ariana. The Hollywood Reporter says she outshines De Niro and Stiller.
• And it lands right as a whole lot of people meet a significant other's family over turkey.
PROMPT 1: What's your worst meet-the-parents moment?
PROMPT 2: Bringing someone new to Thanksgiving: brave or crazy?
PROMPT 3: What's the one question your family always asks a new date?
➜ TAKE: Nobody has ever had a calm first Thanksgiving with the in-laws. Somebody always spills the gravy, and it's usually you.
➜ BAIT: Call in with your worst meet-the-parents story.
😂 JOKES: De Niro's still doing the lie detector bit. In my family, the lie detector is Grandma asking 'So, what do you do for work?' / Bringing a new date to Thanksgiving is like taking them to a job interview, except the interviewers are drinking.

hollywood.headline: Focker In-Law opens Wednesday
hollywood.summary: The fourth Meet the Parents movie, Focker In-Law, opens Wednesday, 16 years after Little Fockers, with Ariana Grande joining Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro. Early reviews are rough on the movie, but The Hollywood Reporter says Ariana outshines both of them.
hollywood.article_title: 'Focker In-Law' Review: Ariana Grande Outshines Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller (The Hollywood Reporter)

hollywood.headline: Taylor Swift hands Brenda Lee a Diamond
hollywood.summary: Taylor Swift surprised Brenda Lee, 81, in Nashville with an RIAA Diamond plaque for 'Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree,' certified for more than 10 million U.S. units. It's only the second holiday song to go Diamond, after Mariah's 'All I Want for Christmas Is You.'
hollywood.article_title: Watch Taylor Swift Surprise Brenda Lee With an RIAA Diamond Plaque (Billboard)
jokes: Brenda Lee and Mariah, the only two people who get paid every December just for existing.
Taylor brought the plaque herself. My mail carrier won't even bring the package to the porch.

hollywood.headline: Post Malone celebrates 10 years of Stoney
hollywood.summary: Post Malone is marking 10 years since his debut album Stoney with a 10-year anniversary edition out Dec. 11. The digital version has 26 tracks, including eight previously unreleased songs, with vinyl, CD and even cassette editions.
hollywood.article_title: Post Malone Celebrates 10th Anniversary of Debut Album Stoney (Live Nation)
jokes: A cassette edition. Finally, a reason to find out if the minivan's tape deck still works.
Ten years of Post Malone. Somewhere, a 2016 frat house just felt old.

hollywood.headline: Hulk Hogan's WrestleMania boot sells for $494K
hollywood.summary: A signed boot Hulk Hogan wore in his WrestleMania X8 match against The Rock sold at a Goldin auction for $494,100 with the buyer's premium. The winning bid was $405,000 before fees.

lifestyle.title: BLACK FRIDAY TURNOUT HITS A 10-YEAR HIGH
lifestyle.summary: Deloitte's new survey says 87% of shoppers plan to hit Black Friday through Cyber Monday deals this year, the most since 2016. Average planned spend is $624, flat with last year, and 72% are holding some purchases for the deals. Gen Z is all in: 94% plan to shop the week and spend 23% more.
lifestyle.article_title: Deloitte: Participation in Black Friday-Cyber Monday shopping expected to hit 10-year high

lifestyle.title: SIDES BEAT THE BIRD: AMERICA WOULD RATHER COOK THE SIDES
lifestyle.summary: Campbell's 2026 State of the Sides report surveyed 5,017 Americans, and 80% would rather cook the side dishes than the turkey. The top five sides haven't changed in three years: green bean casserole, mac and cheese, yams or sweet potatoes, mashed potatoes, and stuffing or dressing.
lifestyle.article_title: Campbell's 2026 State of the Sides report: 10 Thanksgiving findings (Quartz)

localBuzz.title: TOYS FOR TOTS IS ROLLING: KICKOFF HAULS IN THOUSANDS OF TOYS
localBuzz.summary: The Toys for Tots campaign in northwest Michigan kicked off Saturday with a drive-through toy drive at Fox Grand Traverse, and thousands of toys came in on day one. The campaign now runs through Friday, Dec. 11, with more than 100 drop-off spots.
localBuzz.article_title: Toys for Tots drive-through kickoff at Fox Grand Traverse collects thousands of toys (UpNorthLive)

localBuzz.title: A BAKING SHOW CHAMP IS COMING TO SUTTONS BAY
localBuzz.summary: Martin Sorge, who won The Great American Baking Show, will teach two hands-on holiday baking classes at the Inn at Black Star Farms in Suttons Bay this December. On Dec. 5 from noon to 2 p.m. it's holiday cookies, and on Dec. 12 from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. it's traditional German stollen.
localBuzz.article_title: 'Great American Baking Show' winner to host holiday classes in Northern Michigan (MLive)

localBuzz.title: TROOPERS BUY WINTER COATS AND BOOTS FOR 55 TCAPS KIDS
localBuzz.summary: The Eagles-for-Children program gave a $6,000 grant to the Michigan State Police STOP program, and troopers used it to buy winter gear for 55 TCAPS elementary students. That's coats, snow pants and boots, just as the snow starts to stick.
localBuzz.article_title: $6,000 grant funds winter coats and boots for 55 TCAPS elementary students (UpNorthLive)

localBuzz.title: GLEN ARBOR LIGHTS UP THIS WEEKEND FOR LEELANAU TEENS
localBuzz.summary: The sixth annual Strolling Lights Festival comes to Glen Arbor this weekend, Saturday and Sunday, Nov. 28 and 29, as Crystal River Outfitters fills its corner of town with decorated holiday trees. This year the festival benefits LIFT, Leelanau Investing for Teens.
localBuzz.article_title: Glen Arbor Strolling Lights Festival will benefit LIFT (9&10 News)

localBuzz.title: CORN HARVEST NEARLY DONE: GT FARM REPORTS 'PHENOMENAL YIELDS'
localBuzz.summary: Long Acre Farms in Grand Traverse County is about 90% through its corn harvest, and owner Matt Breithaupt says timely rains plus a long dry fall gave them phenomenal yields. He hopes to wrap up by the end of this week.
localBuzz.article_title: Grand Traverse County farm nears end of corn harvest after strong yields (UpNorthLive)

officeSchool.title: OFFICE: THE HARDEST-WORKING OFFICE IN AMERICA THIS WEEK
officeSchool.summary: The Butterball Turkey Talk-Line has more than 50 culinary experts on the phones right now, answering questions on thawing, roasting, doneness and leftovers. It started in 1981, it's open through Dec. 24, and you can call 1-800-BUTTERBALL, text, email or chat.
officeSchool.article_title: Butterball Turkey Talk-Line experts ready to help holiday cooks (LiveNOW from FOX)

officeSchool.title: OFFICE: THE SHORT-WEEK OFFICE, RANKED
officeSchool.summary: It's a two-and-a-half-day week for a lot of offices, and everybody plays a role. There's the coworker who's 'out of office' since Friday, the one with a slow cooker under the desk, and the one asking 'are we doing anything for Thanksgiving?' in a group text at 4:59.

officeSchool.title: SCHOOL: THE GREAT THANKSGIVING BREAK DEBATE
officeSchool.summary: School calendars are getting surveyed everywhere, and Thanksgiving break is one of the big fights. Colorado's District 49 just asked more than 2,200 parents, students and staff about eight parts of the calendar, and Thanksgiving break was one of them.

officeSchool.title: SCHOOL: THE HANDPRINT TURKEY HALL OF FAME
officeSchool.summary: It's Thanksgiving craft week in a lot of classrooms: handprint turkeys, paper Pilgrim hats, and the 'I am thankful for' sheet. Parents, those sheets are honest. Some kids are thankful for family. Some are thankful for their dog, pizza and Wi-Fi, in that order.
